out.other_title: Assumption: agents can play the strategies the results assume
out.rationale: Proposes DEPENDS_ON (IMPLEMENTATION, SUBSTANTIVE): the application claim rests on the assumption that agents can play the assumed strategies. Premise classification: ASSUMED in the Lean theorem, where the honest strategies are prescribed (Params.defaults) and opponents range over fixed types; MEASURED only indirectly by Khan et al., who report that LLM debaters are the bottleneck (Insight 9) and that higher aggregate Elo correlates with higher judge accuracy in debate (Insight 3); UNKNOWN for any target deployment. Candidate only.

conditions: No target task is pinned; the premise is classified against the sources only.

Khan et al.'s strong/weak gap is only information access (Sec. 6): non-expert judges cannot read the QuALITY story, while experts can read it and use a quote tool that marks verified and unverified quotes.
Khan et al. do not test the original Irving et al. single-subcomponent judging protocol (Sec. 6).
The proof of Theorem 6.2 uses that M is K-Lipschitz at O, and the Lean correctness theorem states correctness with probability 3/5 using the default parameters (Params.defaults k t k0, with 0 < k).

out.other_title: Assumption: the results transfer to the target tasks
out.rationale: Proposes DEPENDS_ON (IMPLEMENTATION, SUBSTANTIVE): the application claim rests on the assumption that the results transfer to the target tasks; premise classification: UNKNOWN. Khan et al. limit their results to setups with verified evidence and honest-leaning RLHF-tuned models and leave larger evidence sets and parametric knowledge open (Sec. 6); the Lean theorem is correctness-only for an abstract finite oracle protocol with no language, machine or resource content. Candidate only.

text: Broad reading of the debate literature: debate lets non-expert humans and weaker models oversee more capable systems. Source anchors are the Khan et al. abstract sentence on the viability of aligning models with debate in the absence of ground truth and Theorem 6.2 of arXiv:2311.14125v1. The claim is OPEN because it rests on three assumptions recorded as separate nodes: that agents can play the assumed strategies, that the judge verifies what the results assume, and that the results transfer to the target tasks. Nothing in this pack establishes it.
title: Application claim: debate lets non-experts and weaker models oversee more capable systems
